# Squash and stretch

**The amount of ball stays the same: on paper, the drawing's area stays about the same.** When the ball hits the floor, it flattens and widens: that is **squash**. When it moves fast, it gets longer and thinner in the direction it travels: that is **stretch**. Shorter means wider.

![Three ball shapes of nearly equal area: stretched while falling, round at the top, squashed on the floor](asset:squash_volume)

**On a contact frame, the ball really touches the floor.** Miss by a hair and the whole bounce floats.

This week your ball can stay round. You add squash and stretch in Module 2.

{{deeper}}

**Shape tells the audience what something is made of.** A bowling ball barely squashes. A water balloon squashes a lot. The fall is the same; the material is different, and the audience reads the material from the shape alone. If the ball changes size instead of shape, it stops looking like an object and starts looking like a mistake.
